newsitem.title: NORWAY: FORECAST - Analysts see Oslo Bourse still rising.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Analysts see Oslo Bourse still rising.

text.p: The Norwegian stock exchange is expected to continue to rise in 1997 despite rallying for most of the time so far this year, according to nine analysts polled by Reuters.
The Oslo-based analysts suggested on the average the Total Index would hit 1,165 points at the end of 1997. The maximum forecast was 1,275 and the minimum was 990.
The index, which hit an all-time closing high of 1,128.46 on February 20, stood at about 1,105 in early afternoon trade on Thursday.

"We have forecast the index to rise 22 percent this year, but most of this increase has already been achieved. We are already up 14 percent, so we can expect another seven-eight percent," one analyst said.
Asked why the index was performing so well, he said: "The crown is strong, interest rates are low and foreigners look with confidence to Norway's strong oil-driven economy."
The Oslo Bourse extended trading hours by one hour to 5 p.m. (1600gmt) from March 3 in the hope of attracting more business.

"Interest rates will probably stay around today's level and the crown will remain strong," the analyst said. "There is a danger of a negative correction in the second half. We could see a marked interest rate rise at the end of the year if inflation is higher than expected. Implicit in all this is that the U.S. market stays stable."
Another analyst who also took a bullish view on 1997 said Norwegian blue chip shares were undervalued on a European level.
He said industrial group Norsk Hydro ASA, Norway's largest listed company, could gain 50 crowns this year and that industrial group Kvaerner ASA should reach between 500 and 550 crowns.
Norsk Hydro was traded at about 350 crowns on Thursday afternoon and Kvaerner A stood at about 366 crowns.
"Aker RGI should reach 210 crowns this year," he said. The company's A share was traded at about 184.50 crowns on Thursday afternoon.
The analyst saw metals maker Elkem ASA, whose A share stood at around 122 crowns in the afternoon, sharply up.

"Elkem is completely undervalued. They have a P/E of about eight while 20 would have been more normal. We could see a price of over 200 crowns," the analyst said. "The big question is how quickly this repricing will come about."
Analysts forecast an average target of 1,332 points in 1998 for the Total Index with forecasts swinging from 1,100 to 1,500.
"We see a 10 percent increase in 1998, a relatively moderate forecast," one said. "We expect interest rates to go up at the end of 1997 and there will be a spill-over effect into 1998."
